skillAdvancement.gain: First-time crafts and recipes near the crafter’s current level grant the most skill experience. Trivial recipes eventually stop advancing the skill.
skillAdvancement.suggestedXP: 4 XP for first successful craft, 2 XP for a nontrivial repeat, 1 XP for a difficult failed attempt that produces usable research, 0 XP for trivial mass production.
skillAdvancement.levelCost: Advancing a tradeskill level requires 10 + current level skill XP.
skillAdvancement.specialization: At skill level 10, choose one specialty within the tradeskill. Specialty recipes gain +1 and may unlock unique substitutions.

materialProperties.rule: A property recipe may accept any component of the required tier carrying the listed properties, unless the formula names a specific irreplaceable part.

harvesting.check: Use the creature type’s knowledge skill to identify components, then the relevant gathering tradeskill to remove them.
harvesting.wholeCreatureRule: A successful full harvest normally exposes four to six component categories. The listed bestiary drops are exceptional components, not the only usable remains.
harvesting.partialHarvest: The expedition may take only selected parts, reducing time and weight but forfeiting the remainder.
harvesting.damageSpoilage: The damage type and condition of the corpse can ruin, alter, or improve specific components.
harvesting.sentientRestriction: Humanoid and celestial remains require consent, lawful authority, or explicit dark-path play. Their bodies are not ordinary resource nodes.

preservation.failure: Expired materials lose one quality step per preservation interval and may become contaminated, inert, or dangerous.

stationsAndTime.field: Up to 2 active hours; improvised camp tools; no permanent legendary items.
stationsAndTime.expedition: Up to 8 active hours at a fortified camp or research station.
stationsAndTime.workshop: One to five workdays at a proper dungeon haven or surface facility.
stationsAndTime.haven: One week to one month; requires a named workshop, secure storage, and uninterrupted phases.
stationsAndTime.legacy: More than one month; completed between seasons, by a retired crafter, or through a protected long-term facility.
stationsAndTime.seasonRule: Crafting time represents active work. The 240-hour descent makes long projects strategic commitments rather than free downtime.

economy.pricing: Recommended market value includes consumed materials, labor, rarity, risk, and access. Required tools are not consumed.
economy.commission: Standard commissions require a 50% deposit plus all irreplaceable monster parts.
economy.failureRecovery: Ordinary failure recovers 25% of non-catalyst materials; skilled Salvaging can improve this.
economy.antiLoop: Selling crafted goods below an appropriate market or faction demand avoids infinite-profit loops. Repeated mass production can saturate a local market.
economy.retirement: Retired crafters may maintain workshops, teach formulas, complete legacy projects, and improve starting expedition equipment.

recipeDiscovery.formulaRules: Recipes above skill level 4 normally require a formula, schema, pattern, or documented oral tradition.
recipeDiscovery.experimentRules: Experimentation requires a stated desired result, components with relevant properties, a station, and a research check. Failure creates notes and may reveal partial properties.

passages.text: DECENNIUM DESCENT
CRAFTING BIBLE
Known Descent Edition
433 established formulas • 604 documented materials • 16 tradeskills
Harvest what survives. Preserve what matters. Carry home what changes the world.
Using This Book

This volume contains the player-facing crafting rules and formulas established through the Haven and the first five documented Gate tiers. Tier VI formulas survive only as restricted fragments from the failed Sixth Gate expedition and are not printed here. No formula beyond the Sixth Gate is treated as public knowledge.
The Crafting Loop

Identify a resource, harvest it without ruining the useful anatomy, preserve it, transport it, refine it, obtain or discover a formula, craft the item, determine quality, and then use, sell, study, repair, or salvage the result.
The 100-Day Opening
The dungeon remains open for 2,400 hours. Crafting time is active work, not free downtime. Every hour spent refining, repairing, brewing, or experimenting competes with exploration and extraction.

Formula ID: recipe-3 • Knowledge: established formula
Use Expedition Watches when hours matter. One Watch is eight hours. Every twenty-four-hour day contains three Watches: Morning, Afternoon, and Evening.
Every member must be assigned to one activity during every Watch. A character may Rest instead of joining a team.
### Haven and Downtime Mode
Use days or weeks for recovery, crafting, research, business, training, politics, and preparation. One Haven Turn is normally one day unless the activity states otherwise.
## 2. Core resolution
Roll:
`d20 + ability modifier + proficiency, when trained + circumstance modifiers`
### Difficulty Classes
| Circumstance | DC |
| Routine under pressure | 10 |
| Tier I standard | 12 |
| Tier II standard | 13 |
| Tier III standard | 15 |
| Tier IV standard | 16 |
| Tier V standard | 18 |
| Tier VI documented limit | 19 |
Use +3 DC for a hard version of the task and +6 DC for a severe version. Use -3 DC when preparation or superior tools make the task favorable.
### Degrees of outcome
- **Critical Success:** Total is at least DC + 10.
- **Success:** Total meets or exceeds the DC.
- **Failure:** Total is below the DC.
- **Critical Failure:** Total is at least 10 below the DC.
A natural 20 improves the result by one degree. A natural 1 worsens the result by one degree. It never improves beyond Critical Success or worsens beyond Critical Failure.
### Advantage and disadvantage
Roll two d20s and use the higher result for advantage or the lower result for disadvantage. Multiple sources do not stack. If both apply, they cancel.
### Assistance

A trained assistant who can meaningfully participate grants +1. Up to three assistants may contribute, for a maximum +3. An assistant exposed to the same danger suffers consequences on a Critical Failure.
## 3. Expedition organization
### Equipment Integrity
Important equipment, vehicles, and transport have Integrity 0–3.
- 3: Sound.
- 2: Worn; no penalty.
- 1: Damaged; checks using it suffer -2.
- 0: Broken; unusable until repaired.
A Repair activity restores 1 Integrity on Success and 2 on Critical Success if materials are available.
## 15. Harvesting and salvage
After an encounter, the Resource Team may Harvest or Salvage during the current or next Watch.
- A hurried attempt takes one hour and suffers disadvantage.
- A normal attempt consumes one activity assignment.
- Failure damages or contaminates one recoverable component.
- Critical Failure may expose the team to poison, disease, curse, or Pressure.
Harvested material becomes cargo immediately and must be preserved if Perishable.
During one Haven Turn a character may:

- **Seek Patronage or Information:** Pay an appropriate lifestyle cost and make a social check; Success gains a contact, lead, or audience, while Critical Failure creates rumor, blackmail, or unwanted attention.
- **Secure a License:** Pay the district fee and satisfy the relevant guild or health check to operate legally.
- **Brew a Batch:** Use the crafting formula, ingredients, facility, and one day of work; illegal substances also create Underways Heat.
- **Treat Dependence or Withdrawal:** Spend one day under qualified care to gain advantage on the next recovery check and prevent one ordinary withdrawal escalation.
